judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble is a straightforward identification of parties, but it treats "Fund" and "Plan" as interchangeable labels for the same thing, which is a latent definitional slippage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 1.20 and 1.22 carefully distinguish the "Plan" (the rules) from the "Trust Fund" (the assets), so the preamble's equation of the two sits awkwardly with Article 1; Amendment No. 4 also replaces this preamble entirely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short recital in ordinary language; nothing in "establish the Plan and require periodic Employer contributions" carries two readings on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the CBAs "establish the Plan," whereas Section 1.20 and Section 4.2 make the Plan a set of rules adopted and amended by the Board, a mild recital-versus-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely narrative recital about what the CBAs contemplate; no operative term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 3 in fact has the Association (not the Union) appoint Employer Trustees and the Union appoint Union Trustees, so the recital's shorthand is imprecise but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Exclusive purpose of providing pension and retirement benefits" is a familiar formula, though "exclusive" is doing real work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2 says "certain pension and related benefits" and Section 5.3 charges administrative expenses to the Fund, so the recital's narrower "exclusive purpose" is slightly out of step with the operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dated historical recital of the trustees' intent to restate; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2's definition of the Agreement as amended and restated from time to time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital cites "Paragraph 18 of the Trust Agreement" as the amendment power, a citation that has no counterpart in the restated instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The operative amendment power is Section 10.1 (with the provisos in 10.1(a)-(c)) and Section 10.2; a recital pointing to a vanished Paragraph 18 is a classic recital-versus-operative mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration boilerplate with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in the instrument turns on this recital of consideration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "unless the context otherwise requires" qualifier lets any defined term be displaced by context, which is a small but real source of interpretive play.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 12.7, which imports Plan definitions "except as otherwise expressly provided," giving two overlapping definitional priority rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defining "Administrator" as "the Board, or any individual or other person duly authorized by the Board" is broad but not genuinely ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.6 makes the Board the ERISA "administrator" while Section 7.1 (garbled) contemplates an Administrator distinct from the Board, so the two roles blur.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional cross-reference to the instrument itself; plain and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the preamble and Section 10.1's amendment mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition names the "Publishers' Association of New York," dropping "City" from the entity's actual name — a small mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble, Section 12.8(d) and the signature block all say "Publishers' Association of New York City," so the defined term does not match the party as named elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Both the Chairman and Secretary of the Board" leaves open whether they must act jointly or each qualifies alone, and the trailing "(or their duly authorized agents)" widens the class further.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.15 requires the Chairman and Secretary together to execute documents while Section 12.6 makes an instrument signed by the Chairman alone conclusive, so who is truly "authorized" is not uniform across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition defers to "the terms of the Plan" for who qualifies, which is definite even if it is not self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.2 and Section 12.15, which likewise make Plan terms controlling for entitlement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise definition tied to ERISA sections 402(a)(2) and 3(16)(A); little room to argue about its wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the Board the ERISA "administrator" while Section 1.1 and Section 7.1 create a separate "Administrator" office, a mild overlap of roles.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined "Code" is the "Internal Revenue Code of 1936," which does not exist; the intended reference is plainly 1986, a mechanical error in a term used throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.3, 4.4, 10.1(b) and 5.7 all hinge on Code sections 401(a), 501(a) and 4975, so an incorrect Code year ripples through the instrument, though the correction is obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Or other written agreement between an Employer and the Union, which is in force and effect and is acceptable to the Board" makes the category turn on an unstated standard of acceptability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.13 defines Employer by reference to a CBA and Section 2.4 requires an approved CBA, so whether an unapproved agreement creates an obligation to contribute is left circular.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is long but definite; the incorporation "to the extent not inconsistent with the terms of this Agreement" is a standard priority rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Board's disclaimer of liability for Collective Trust trustees sits alongside Section 5.7's prudence duty and Section 7.2(13)'s duty to monitor, a familiar tension but not a squarely stated conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Containing at least one Employer Trustee and one Union Trustee" is a clear minimum requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(b) requires each Committee to have "an equal number of Employer Trustees and Union Trustees," which forbids compositions that Section 1.10's minimum would permit — a direct inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: coverage turns on employment plus a CBA requiring contributions for the individual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 1.13, 2.4 and 9.1, all of which key obligations to the CBA.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition folds two distinct roles — Corporate Trustee and custodian — into one term joined by "and/or," leaving the Custodian's status uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.12 speaks of the Corporate Trustee as a separate sole trustee while Sections 5.12 and 8.1(b) treat the Custodian as a mere holder, so the merged definition does not map onto how the term is used.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any employer required to contribute" is circular in that the obligation is what defines the class, but the CBA reference gives it content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.4 makes participation depend on executing a Board-approved CBA and designating an effective date, so whether a non-signatory can be an "Employer" is not resolved between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference definition; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(a) is amended by Amendment No. 4, but the definition tracks whatever 3.3(a) says.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard statutory definition; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently throughout; ERISA supremacy is also confirmed by Sections 2.3 and 12.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined entirely by reference to ERISA section 404(b) and 29 C.F.R. 2550.404b-1; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5(p) uses the term consistently with the same regulatory requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Able to verify with a reasonable degree of certainty the identity of the sender" is a soft standard, but it is a familiar one and the core requirement (signed writing) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Section 1.4's Authorized Person definition and Section 8.6's Instructions; no conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully enumerated (a)/(b)(1)-(3) qualifications tracking ERISA and the Advisers Act; little interpretive play.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states that an Investment Manager "has acknowledged in writing" fiduciary status, whereas Section 8.3 makes obtaining that acknowledgment merely permissive ("may require").

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple segregation definition; "segregated by the Trustees" is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.1(b) has the Board or the Custodian do the segregating, a trivial variance rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: the Plan is the Board-adopted rules on eligibility and benefits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble equates "Fund" and "Plan," and Recital 2 says the CBAs establish the Plan, both slightly at odds with this Board-adopted-rules definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All Trust Fund securities of any and every kind ... including, but not limited to" followed by eleven enumerated categories is the paradigm general-catch-all-against-specifics structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 grants powers over "Securities or other property," so the breadth of the definition is largely absorbed by the parallel "other property" language elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear asset-based definition covering segregated and pooled holdings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.9, 1.19, 5.1 and 5.12; the only friction is the preamble's use of "Fund" to mean the Plan.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical "(if such Successor Trustees have been appointed)" and the phrase "when acting as Trustees" are awkward and leave the successors' status conditional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.11 vests successors with full powers on acceptance, so the conditional definition is at most redundant rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "And any affiliates thereof" is an undefined extension of the party's identity, though the named local is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble also uses "affiliates" collectively, so the instrument is internally consistent even if the boundary of "affiliates" is soft.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to Section 3.3(b); nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.8 and 3.10 add that Union Trustees are the Union's incumbent officers, which supplements rather than contradicts the definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line naming provision with no operative reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same name appears in the preamble and Section 9.3; no divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Certain pension and related benefits" leaves the boundary of "related benefits" undefined while the sentence is framed as an "exclusive purpose."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recital 4 says the exclusive purpose is "pension and retirement benefits," and Section 4.1(a) permits "such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine" — three formulations of the same limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming language — anything inconsistent with the Code or ERISA means "this Agreement shall be deemed amended in such fashion as will implement the purposes of this Trust" — states no determinate content for the deemed amendment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a whole-instrument override that interacts with Sections 5.9(b), 9.5(b) and 10.1, any of which a party could argue is automatically rewritten by operation of this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any contributing Employer acceptable to the Trustees may participate" makes acceptance discretionary and unstandardised, and the three lettered steps read as conditions without saying they are exclusive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.13 defines Employer without reference to Board approval and Section 2.5 deems obligations onto an Employer, so whether these steps are the only route into the Trust is genuinely unsettled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall be deemed to have ... agreed to be bound unconditionally" to all present and future amendments is a strong deeming clause whose trigger is never stated in the section itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1's closing sentence says nothing in the Trust Agreement changes the terms of any CBA, which cuts against deeming employers unconditionally bound to Board-made amendments imposing new charges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is misnumbered "3.2" and provides an odd-numbered board — two Employer and three Union Trustees — while the closing sentence points to Section 3.4 for appointment mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.2(b) lets "any four Trustees" call a meeting and Section 10.1(c) forbids unequal voting power, and Amendment No. 4 replaces this text with a two-and-two board, so the composition rule does not sit still across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional acceptance-of-trust clause; the duties it recites are stated elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Sections 3.4 and 3.11 on written acceptance; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of named individuals; nothing to construe in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 4 replaces this list wholesale, so the original text is superseded rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As soon as practicable" is soft, but the obligation (file written appointments and acceptances) is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1 says appointment "shall be governed by the provisions of Section 3.4," yet 3.4 addresses only successor appointments, so the cross-reference over-promises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite tenure provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6, 3.7, 3.8 and 6.1(a)'s officer terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence deems a Trustee resigned when "the Contributing Employer which designated him" ceases to contribute, but Trustees are designated by the Association and the Union, not by individual employers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That mismatch runs directly against Sections 3.1, 3.3, 3.7 and 3.9, which vest designation of Employer Trustees in the Association, leaving the deemed-resignation trigger inoperable as written.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Removal "at any time, with or without cause" by written instrument is about as definite as such clauses get.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.6's reference to the "Contributing Employer that designated him" cuts against 3.7's Association-only removal power, a small friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading is "Removal of Union Trustees" but the text mostly prescribes who holds the office, and it supplies no removal mechanism at all except "by operation of law."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.10 says the Union's principal officer designates successors while this section says successors are "elected from the full-time officers," and Section 3.7 gives the Association an at-will removal right with no Union counterpart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean mechanism: certificate in writing signed by an authorized Association officer.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 3.1, 3.3(a) and 3.11 without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section contradicts itself in one sentence: the principal officer "shall designate a successor Union Trustee by filing ... in which case a Successor Union Trustee shall be elected from the full-time officers of the Union."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.8 (and its Amendment No. 4 replacement) says Union Trustees are automatically the Union's incumbent officers, a third mechanism that cannot be reconciled with either designation or election.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional vesting provision for successors; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Sections 3.4, 3.9 and 3.10 on written acceptance and filing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is materially incomplete — "Notwithstanding such transfer, the Board ... functions under the Plan" has no verb, and (d) similarly drops words — so the retained-responsibility carve-out cannot be read as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.12 defines the Custodian as the "Corporate Trustee" while 3.12(b) makes the Corporate Trustee a sole trustee of a separate trust and forever discharges the Trustees, which is hard to square with Sections 5.7 and 7.2(13).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (a) gives "full authority" over benefits, then limits it to "pension, retirement, and such other related benefits as the Board may from time to time determine" — a catch-all against enumerated specifics whose reach is left to the Board.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2's "certain pension and related benefits" and Recital 4's "pension and retirement benefits" state the same limit differently, and 4.1(c)'s employer indemnity sits against Section 5.9's Fund-side indemnity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences; the power to "amend or otherwise modify the Plan (from time to time) or terminate the Plan (at any time)" is plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 conditions amendment on a unanimous Board vote and three provisos, and Section 10.3 sets out specific termination routes, so 4.2's unqualified "at any time" power is broader than Article 10 allows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence permissive statement; "may (but need not necessarily)" is redundant but not ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Sections 4.1(b), 5.4 and 5.5(k) on insurance contracts without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lettered conditions are scrambled — clause (c) appears after the operative sentence and clause (b) is truncated — so the triggers for returning a contribution cannot be read in order.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.2 forbids any return or diversion of Fund assets to Contributing Employers "except as otherwise provided in Section 10.3," making no allowance for the refunds Section 4.4 authorises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The anti-alienation text is heavily garbled, with clauses interleaved and the final sentence authorising the Board to "terminate or postpone" payments "to the spouse, children and relatives" of the payee, which does not follow from what precedes it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its carve-outs for QDROs and Plan provisions align with Section 12.15 and Section 4.2, so the trouble is internal to the section rather than a conflict with another provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear designation of the Board as recipient of contributions with all right, title and interest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.15's denial of any interest in Fund property to employees and Section 5.12's custody rules fit comfortably with this provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short directive that defers wholly to the written Plan; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly cross-refers to Section 4.2 and is consistent with Section 7.2(17)-(18).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All reasonable and necessary expenses ... including, but not limited to" seven enumerated categories is a general-versus-specific structure resting on the elastic word "reasonable."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(8) separately assigns approval of the same expenses to the Board and Section 9.4(a) says collection costs are paid from the Fund while 9.4(b) charges them to the delinquent employer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional insurance-contract authority clause with a clear non-party disclaimer for carriers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1(b), 4.3 and 5.5(k); no competing provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant runs "in its sole and absolute discretion" over twenty-five enumerated powers and closes with (y), a catch-all to "perform all acts (whether or not expressly authorized herein)" — precisely the general-against-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That absolute discretion has to be squared with Section 5.7's prudence and diversification duty and with Section 8.4, which withholds subsections (j) through (y) from Investment Managers by a garbled cross-reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (b) — "two or more Trustees (of which there shall be an equal number of Employer Trustees and Union Trustees)" — is definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.10 defines a Committee as one containing "at least one Employer Trustee and one Union Trustee," which permits unequal committees that 5.6(b) forbids; the two cannot both be applied.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prudent-person and diversification language tracks ERISA section 404 almost verbatim, so its meaning is supplied by settled statutory usage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is hard to reconcile with Section 5.5's "sole and absolute discretion" free of state-law investment limits, with Section 5.8's conclusive-reliance protection, and with Section 5.9(b)'s exoneration for "any error of judgment."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "May accept the same as conclusive evidence of the truth and accuracy" with "no duty to make any investigation or inquiry" is a strong but plainly worded protection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against Section 5.7's prudence standard and Section 9.9's audit rights, and its opening lacks the "except as provided by ERISA" carve-out that Section 5.9 contains.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (b) exonerates Trustees from "any error of judgment or ... any loss arising out of any act or omission," which on its face swallows every duty the instrument imposes, and (d)'s "except as may otherwise reimbursed by insurance" is missing a word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanket exoneration cannot be harmonised with Section 5.7's standard of care or Section 5.11's fiduciary-breach insurance, and the opening "Except as may otherwise be provided by ERISA" invites argument about how much survives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite bonding requirement pegged to ERISA section 412 with a discretionary top-up.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.3's expense provisions; nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To the extent not precluded by ERISA, the Fund shall purchase and maintain" is a clear mandatory obligation with a statutory limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section 5.9 and is consistent with it; ERISA section 410(b) supplies the boundary the clause itself acknowledges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deposit and signature-authority rules stated with specifics (FDIC/SIPC institutions; two Trustees, one from each side).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Sections 5.13, 5.15 and 7.2 on delegation; no competing signature rule was found other than Section 12.6's Chairman-alone conclusiveness.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Ministerial powers or duties" is an undefined line that the section itself does not draw, and the boundary between ministerial and fiduciary acts is exactly what parties fight about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.6(a) allows delegation of "fiduciary responsibilities" to Committees and Section 5.5(r) allows delegation of operational duties, so 5.13's narrower limit does not describe the instrument's actual practice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Complete authority, in its sole and absolute discretion, to construe the terms of the Plan or this Agreement," with all decisions "final and binding upon all parties affected thereby," is the kind of reservation whose scope is routinely contested.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its finality is qualified by the opening "Except as may otherwise be provided herein," and it must be read against Section 6.6's deadlock arbitration and Section 9.10's mandatory withdrawal-liability arbitration, which take construction questions away from the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A workable execution provision naming the Chairman and Secretary and allowing resolution-based delegation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.6 makes any instrument executed by the Chairman alone conclusive in favour of third parties, which does not match 5.15's two-signature default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Officer terms "commence on the date of their election" though no election procedure is prescribed anywhere, and "continues" is a grammatical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 6.3 and 6.4 govern voting and quorum but never provide for electing officers, leaving 6.1's mechanism unsupported by the rest of Article 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (b) lets "any four Trustees" call a special meeting, an oddly high threshold stated without regard to how many Trustees exist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1 provides for only five Trustees and Amendment No. 4 reduces the Board to four, so "any four Trustees" becomes all or nearly all of them, making the special-meeting right largely illusory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence quorum rule with a fixed number from each side; nothing ambiguous in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With only two Employer Trustees under Section 3.1 (and two Union Trustees after Amendment No. 4), the quorum requires the entire Board, which interacts oddly with Section 6.4(d)'s "lack of a quorum at two consecutive meetings" trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Unit voting with unanimity between the two units is stated clearly, and (d) defines deadlock by example ("including a motion to table").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes deadlocks to Section 6.6 arbitration, consistent with that section, though Section 5.14's "final and binding" Board discretion assumes decisions the unanimity rule may never produce.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: keep minutes, they need not be verbatim, circulate copies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere in Article 6 or Article 11 competes with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (a) breaks off mid-sentence at "petition the United States District Court for the Southern" and the deadlock trigger relies on the same "lack of a unanimous vote" formula used in 6.4.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This arbitration route for Board deadlocks sits alongside Section 9.10's separate withdrawal-liability arbitration and Section 5.14's finality clause, three different decision-making channels that must be kept apart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence is broken — "Where the Administrator is a Trust Fund, subject to the terms of this Agreement" has no predicate — and the section is misnumbered "9.2," so the Administrator's responsibilities are introduced by a sentence that says nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.1 defines the Administrator as possibly being the Board itself, while this section presupposes a separate person, and item (c) gives the Administrator benefit-eligibility determinations that Section 7.2(15) assigns to the Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eighteen-item list introduced by "without limitation" and closing with item (18)'s general "those functions ... which the Board deems necessary and appropriate" — general catch-all against enumerated specifics, with several items badly garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Items (1) and (2) claim a right to "amend, modify or terminate this Agreement at any time," which is broader than Section 10.1's unanimity requirement and provisos and than Section 10.2's flat prohibition on diversion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three clear subsections on appointing, segregating and self-directing; the only slip is "the Securities of other property."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is echoed almost word for word by Section 8.4(b), which is redundancy rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite mechanics: a Board certificate, an effective date, a written agreement and mutually agreed compensation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to Section 8.8's guidelines and matches Section 7.2(12)-(14); no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, permissive ("may require"), with two precise ERISA references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.18 defines an Investment Manager as one who "has acknowledged in writing to the Board" its fiduciary status, making the acknowledgment a definitional precondition that 8.3 treats as optional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out — powers of Section 5.5 "except subsections (3) through (y)" — misidentifies the starting subsection (there is no (3) in 5.5), so the scope of what the Investment Manager may not do is unreadable as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5's lettered list runs (a) through (y) and Section 8.4(b) mirrors 8.1(c), so the defective cross-reference is the only thing that fixes the boundary between Board and Manager authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Agreement" plus a full liability disclaimer, qualified only by assets over which the Board "has specifically assumed investment management duties."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(13) obliges the Board to monitor and evaluate Investment Managers and Section 5.7 imposes prudence, so a blanket "notwithstanding" disclaimer is in tension with duties the instrument elsewhere imposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short authority-to-trade provision expressly made "subject to the terms of the investment management agreement."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.4 and 8.8; the subordination to the management agreement resolves any overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall be the sole responsibility of the Board" is ambiguous between responsibility for setting the terms and legal responsibility for the Manager's conduct.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read the second way it collides head-on with Section 8.5, which says the Board is not "responsible or liable for any acts or omissions of any Investment Manager."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Wholly permissive ("may (but need not)") with an express anti-inference sentence; clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces Sections 8.5 and 8.2(c) rather than contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — "Nothing in this Trust Agreement shall be deemed to change, alter or amend any of the terms or provisions of any such agreement" — is a broad subordination whose reach is not stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is difficult to reconcile with Section 2.5, which deems Employers bound unconditionally to the Trust and all amendments, and with Sections 9.4-9.7, which impose interest and liquidated damages that no CBA need contain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two clauses tying effectiveness and duration of contributions to the CBA; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Sections 9.1 and 1.8, and the CBA-driven duration is consistent with Section 1.13's definition of Employer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A payee-and-form provision; "in the manner and form prescribed by the Board" is delegation, not ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.9 supplies the remittance-report mechanics it contemplates; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subsection (a) says collection costs "shall be paid from the Fund" and then reverses course with "Notwithstanding the preceding sentence," while (b)'s penalty is "the greater of interest on, or twenty percent of, the unpaid contributions" — a comparison of an unspecified interest amount against a percentage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assesses interest "at a rate calculated in accordance with Section 9.5," but Section 9.5(b) states a flat 18 percent rate rather than any calculation method, and Amendment No. 2 makes even that rate discretionary.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of recoverable items is introduced by "including, but not limited to," so the fixed 18 percent rate sits inside an open-ended catch-all of "any expenses incurred in effectuating such payment."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.4(a) and 9.7(b)-(c) both cross-refer to "the method set forth in Section 9.5" although 9.5(b) supplies only a rate, and Amendment No. 2 replaces this text with a discretionary rate, so which rate governs a given delinquency is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines "unpaid contributions" by reference to this Agreement, any CBA "or other agreement," and any Board rules — a broad composite label, though the ERISA hook is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same defined phrase is then used in Section 9.7 without repeating the definition, so the breadth adopted here carries into the court-award provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The five lettered items track ERISA section 502(g)(2) closely, ending with (e)'s open "such other legal or equitable relief as the court deems appropriate."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Items (b) and (c) invoke "the method set forth in Section 9.5," which contains a rate rather than a method, and 9.7(c)'s flat 20 percent differs in form from Section 9.4(b)'s "greater of" formulation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional non-waiver clause; the reference to "Article IX" and then "Article 9" in one sentence is a cosmetic inconsistency only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the Union's separate enforcement rights alongside Sections 9.5 and 9.6, which is complementary rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All records deemed necessary by such persons" makes the audit's scope depend on the auditor's own judgment, and "may at any time" sets no limitation period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.1(b) opens the Fund's own books to each Contributing Employer, and Section 9.4 governs the consequences of what an audit reveals; the two fit together without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause forbids litigation of withdrawal-liability claims and then closes by preserving the Fund's right to sue when a claimant fails to arbitrate in time, so "shall not become the subject of litigation in the courts" is only partly true on the section's own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also directs New York law "to the extent not superceded by ERISA," overlapping Section 12.2, and stands apart from Section 6.6's arbitration and Section 5.14's finality clause, leaving the boundaries between the three regimes to be worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "At any time and in any manner" is then hedged by three provisos, including (a)'s "not inconsistent with the purposes for which the Fund was established," a standard with no fixed content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2(1)-(2) states the amendment right without any of these provisos, Section 4.2 lets the Board amend the Plan at will, and Section 10.2 imposes a further prohibition, so three provisions describe the same power differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear prohibition on diverting the Fund, subject to a single stated exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exception is limited to Section 10.3, yet Section 4.4 expressly authorises returning mistaken or non-deductible contributions to Employers — a return that 10.2 on its face forbids.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three termination routes are enumerated and (b)'s wind-up direction is definite, though "any remaining surplus in a manner consistent, in their opinion, with this Agreement" leaves the distribution to Trustee opinion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (b)'s "[u]nder no circumstances shall any portion of the corpus or income ... revert or accrue to the benefit of any Employer" is hard to square with Section 4.4's employer refunds, which Section 10.2 routes through this very section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Its records shall constitute the official records of the Plan and Trust Fund for all purposes" is a strong evidentiary rule, but it is plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The opening "[u]nless otherwise delegated" defers to Sections 5.13, 7.1(g) and 8.x, and Section 11.2 supplies the valuation rule 11.1(c) presupposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Such commercially acceptable valuation method or methods determined by the Board" leaves the valuation standard entirely to the Board's own choice, which is exactly the sort of open standard parties argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.1(c) requires the Board to maintain information enabling fair market valuation and Section 5.7 imposes prudence, so the discretion here is bounded elsewhere but not contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The New York city metropolitan area" is a geographically fuzzy phrase, and the Board is "deemed to be located at that address" although no address is given in the sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.8's notice addresses (as amended twice) supply the actual location, and Sections 6.6(e) and 9.10 fix New York City as the arbitration situs, so the instrument is broadly consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional New York choice-of-law clause with an express ERISA-preemption limit; the terms are standard and well understood.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.10 separately applies New York law to withdrawal-liability arbitrations "to the extent not superceded by ERISA," which duplicates rather than contradicts this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard counterparts boilerplate; no term with two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.2 also refers to signing "any counterpart or copy hereof," consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It directs that headings not be used in construing the Agreement and supplies number and gender rules; it is itself an interpretive instruction rather than an ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matters because headings elsewhere mislead — Section 3.8 is headed "Removal of Union Trustees" but prescribes who serves — so this clause is the tool for resolving that mismatch rather than a source of conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence designating the Board as agent for service; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12.1 deems the Board located at the Fund's principal office, which supports rather than conflicts with this designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A third-party protection clause making certificates conclusive as to three enumerated matters; the enumeration is closed and the language is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes instruments "executed by the Chairman" alone conclusive, whereas Section 5.15 requires the Chairman and Secretary (or a resolution-based delegation) to bind the Board, and Section 1.4 defines Authorized Person as "both the Chairman and Secretary."

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and clear on its face: Plan definitions carry over "except as otherwise expressly provided herein."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 1 already defines many of the same terms and its preface says definitions apply "unless the context otherwise requires," so two different priority rules govern the same words, and the Plan is a document the Board may amend unilaterally under Section 4.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision's closing sentence is cut off mid-clause ("as of the date on which it is"), leaving the deemed-receipt rule incomplete, and "delivered in writing" versus "deposited by first-class mail" set two different moments of effectiveness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendments No. 1 and No. 3 replace subsections (a)-(d) and rename the addressee "Fund Director" rather than the "Fund Administrator" used here and the "Administrator" defined in Section 1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extracted text begins mid-sentence — "the Board) or any person claiming by or through them" — so the class of persons denied any interest cannot be identified from the provision itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its rule that no one is entitled to payment "unless and until the Board determines" eligibility reinforces Sections 5.14 and 12.16, but it also has to coexist with Section 4.2's written Plan entitlements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-employment-right and no-equity-interest clause, closing with "except as set forth in the Plan."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reads together with Section 12.15 and Section 4.2 without friction; the Plan carve-out preserves participants' actual benefit rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Continue in effect without limit as to time" subject to Article 10 is plain and self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly defers to Article 10, and Section 10.3(a)(3)'s automatic termination fits within that deferral.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recital says "the Plan is hereby amended" when the operative text amends Section 12.8(b) of the Trust Agreement — a mechanical error about which instrument is being changed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10.1 permits amendment of both the Agreement and the Plan by unanimous Board vote, and Section 1.20 keeps the two documents distinct, so the mislabel matters for what this amendment actually altered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement text ends "18 percent per annum or such other interest rate that the Trustees deem appropriate given [the] circumstances," an open-ended rate with no stated ceiling, standard or trigger, sitting inside an "including, but not limited to" list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.4(a), 9.7(b) and 9.7(c) all compute interest "in accordance with the method set forth in Section 9.5," so replacing the fixed rate with a discretionary one leaves those cross-references without a determinate method.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward address substitution, though the text for subsection (d) breaks off after "620 E ighth Avenue" with no city, state or zip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes Section 12.8 and Amendment No. 1 and, like Amendment No. 1, uses "Fund Director" where the Agreement says "Administrator," a naming mismatch with Section 1.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stray "2. the following:" is embedded in the middle of the amendment, and the replacement preamble still describes the Fund as "the 'Fund' or 'Plan'" despite Article 1 treating those as different things.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names four Trustees, consistent with the amended Section 3.1's two-and-two board, but leaves Sections 6.2(b) ("any four Trustees") and 6.3's quorum operating on a four-person Board.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence reads "The appointment of Trustees shall be selected by the provisions of Section 3.4," a grammatical error introduced by the amendment where the original said "governed by."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reducing the Board to four Trustees makes Section 6.2(b)'s "any four Trustees" special-meeting right require unanimity and makes Section 6.3's quorum the entire Board, and Section 3.4 still addresses only successor appointments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of two names per side; nothing to construe beyond an OCR break in one name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the amended Section 3.1 and the amended preamble, and Sections 1.14 and 1.25 track whatever 3.3 says.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading remains "Removal of Union Trustees" while the text prescribes who holds office, and "vice president/secretary treasurer" compresses two offices into one designation of uncertain scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.10 still says the Union's principal officer "shall designate" a successor who "shall be elected from the full-time officers," which cannot be reconciled with automatic service by incumbent officers under this amended section.
